session_1.text: I think both are wonderful companions. Do you have a favorite?

session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.speaker: AI

session_1.speaker: AI

session_1.text: Oh yes. Chips, salsa, the usual treats.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Sounds delicious! Snacking and spreadsheets—that's multitasking.
session_1.speaker: AI

session_1.text: Haha, you know me well.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.speaker: AI

session_1.text: No surprises. Just that the file to read data from is CS161_Class_Roster.xlsx when it comes to student details.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Crystal clear! CS161_Class_Roster.xlsx will be my go-to reference file.
session_1.speaker: AI

session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Just update me if anything changes!
session_1.speaker: AI

session_1.text: Definitely. For now, let’s just keep things simple.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Sounds perfect. Simplicity is underrated.
session_1.speaker: AI

session_1.text: Agreed. Catch you after lunch for more work.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: I'll be ready! Enjoy your break, Alice.
session_1.speaker: AI

session_1.text: Thanks! Signing off for now.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Take care and see you soon!

session_2.text: Morning, time for another work day! Any motivational quotes for me?

session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: Speaking of which, when filtering a student list, should I include all freshmen or just ones from a specific department?
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: It depends on your purpose. If you want more focus, combining criteria like both class year and major narrows the field.
session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: That's true. And avoids a giant, overwhelming list!
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Exactly. Filtering by both year and major gets you the most relevant data.
session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: I think that's the right idea. So, only include students who are freshmen AND have math as their major for this list.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Got it. Both 'Freshman' in academic standing and 'Math' as the major, right?
session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: Yep! Both conditions need to be true, or else they don't make the cut.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Understood. Only math majors who are also freshmen will appear in your new list.
session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: Perfect! I'll jot that down so I don't forget.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Great idea. If you ever want to double-check your filter logic, just let me know.
session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: Will do. Oh, what else could you filter for, besides year and major?
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: That's a lot of options. Too many filters and I’ll spend more time filtering than working!
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: True! Keeping it to just the key filters helps streamline things.
session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: Right! I’ll stick to just Freshman with Math this time.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Sensible. That should be a nice, concise subset.
session_2.speaker: AI

session_2.text: Let’s see how small a group that ends up being.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Yep! Easy to read that way.

session_2.text: Exactly. Happy to double-check the logic when you’re ready to process the list.
